Private practice can be a lonely job.

Most of the week it’s you, a client and a closed door. MTC gets local clinicians into the same room a few times a season, so you have colleagues to call when a case gets hard, and names you trust when a client needs a referral.

Therapists, psychologists, social workers, counselors, grad students and associates are all welcome, along with the dietitians, coaches and bodyworkers our clients see too.

Come on your own. Most people do.

Meet Jen JosephFounder, Montclair Therapy Collective

PsyD, CGP, PMH-C. Licensed psychologist in New York and New Jersey.

Jen has been a psychologist for more than twenty years. She sees individuals, couples and groups at her office on Park Street and works from a modern psychoanalytic orientation. Her specialties include chronic pain, perinatal mental health, and adult children of parents with mental illness, and she supervises first-year doctoral students.

Groups run through almost everything she does. She’s been a Certified Group Psychotherapist since 2011, finished the program at the Center for Group Studies in New York in 2020, and leads supervision and consultation groups where therapists bring their hardest cases and work through them together.

MTC takes that same idea out of the office. Clinicians do better work when they aren’t doing it alone.

Frequently asked questions

Who can come to MTC events?

Psychotherapists and allied professionals in and around Montclair. That includes licensed therapists, psychologists, social workers and counselors, grad students and associates, and professionals like dietitians, coaches and bodyworkers who work alongside therapists.

Do I need to be a member?

No. Events are open to any clinician in the area, and you register for each one on Luma. A paid membership is planned alongside the directory, with member pricing on events and a listing in the directory.

What does it cost?

It depends on the event. Networking nights have a $10 suggested donation and workshops usually a $15 suggested donation. Each event’s Luma page has the details.

Do the workshops offer CE credit?

Some do. When CE is available it comes through the presenter’s approved provider, and the event listing will say so.

I don’t know anyone. Should I still come?

Yes. Most people come on their own, and the events are set up for meeting new people.

When will the directory open?

Once enough members are ready to be listed. Join the list below and check “Being listed in the directory” to hear first and save your spot.

Can I lead a workshop or host a gathering?

Jen would love to hear your idea. Reach out through the contact page or Instagram.
